Lymphocyte profiles in mediastinal lymph nodes may reflect the immune status of patients with sarcoidosis. Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) is useful for the diagnosis of diseases with mediastinal lymphadenopathy including sarcoidosis. The purpose of this study was to determine lymphocyte profiles of lymph nodes in sarcoidosis by analyzing EBUS-TBNA samples. We prepared single cell suspensions from EBUS-TBNA samples of mediastinal lymph nodes from patients with sarcoidosis or lung cancer and analyzed surface markers (CD3, CD4, CD8, CD19, CD25) and FoxP3 expression in the resultant lymphocytes using flow cytometry. We studied 26 patients with sarcoidosis and 16 with lung cancer with mediastinal lymph node metastases. In sarcoidosis, the CD4/CD8 ratio was significantly more elevated in lymph nodes than in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (P<0.001), although both were strongly correlated. The CD4/CD8 ratio was significantly higher in stage I than in stage II both in the BAL fluid and lymph nodes. When compared with lung cancer lymph node metastasis, the CD4/CD8 ratio was significantly higher in sarcoidosis, whereas the CD3/CD19 ratio was significantly higher in lung cancer. The proportion of regulatory T cells (CD4 + , CD25 + , FoxP3 high ) did not differ between sarcoidosis and lung cancer samples. Lymphocyte profiles in mediastinal lymphadenopathy can be analyzed by flow cytometry of EBUS-TBNA samples. These findings might help elucidate the immunopathology of sarcoidosis. Introduction Although CD4-positive T-lymphocytes are thought to play an important role in sarcoidosis, its pathogenesis has not been fully elucidated, although the excessive activation of CD4 positive T lymphocytes is a hallmark of sarcoidosis [ 1 ]. An elevated ratio of CD4/CD8 positive T-lymphocytes in bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluid is suggestive for sarcoidosis diagnosis [ 2 ]. However, little is known about lymphocyte dynamics in the affected lymph nodes in sarcoidosis. Although previous reports reported the lymphocyte profile in sarcoidosis lymph nodes including the CD4/CD8 ratio, the results were inconsistent among these reports [ 3 , 4 ]. With recent advances in respiratory endoscopic technologies including endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration (EBUS-TBNA), the diagnostic accuracy for various mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathies has been markedly improved. EBUS-TBNA samples are available for histological diagnosis and for molecular diagnosis or immunohistochemical analyses [ 5 , 6 , 7 ]. Recent studies showed gastrointestinal endoscopic ultrasound guided fine needle aspiration (FNA) biopsy is an established procedure for the diagnosis of lymphoma [ 8 , 9 , 10 ]. FNA-biopsy samples can be used for flow cytometric analysis, which is essential for the diagnosis of lymphoma. The purpose of this study was to analyze lymphocyte profiles in sarcoidosis lymph nodes by analyzing EBUS-TBNA samples using flow cytometry. We investigated the ratio of T-lymphocytes/B-lymphocytes, CD4/CD8 T-lymphocytes and regulatory T cells (Treg)/CD4 T-lymphocytes in affected lymph nodes of sarcoidosis patients. Comparative analyses of lymphocyte profiles in BAL fluid and lymph nodes were also performed. To elucidate the specific lymphocyte profile of sarcoidosis, we also compared the lymphocyte profile between sarcoidosis lymph nodes and lung cancer metastatic lymph nodes.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated lymphocyte profiles (CD4/CD8 ratio, CD3/CD19 ratio, and regulatory T cells) in mediastinal lymph nodes and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid from sarcoidosis and lung cancer patients using EBUS-TBNA samples and flow cytometry. The findings revealed significantly elevated CD4/CD8 ratios in sarcoidosis lymph nodes compared to BAL fluid and lung cancer metastases, and a higher ratio in stage I sarcoidosis than stage II, aiding in differential diagnosis and understanding disease immunopathology.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Diagnostic analysis of lymphocyte profiles using flow cytometry on samples obtained via Endobronchial Ultrasound-guided Transbronchial Needle Aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) from mediastinal lymph nodes and Bronchoalveolar Lavage (BAL) fluid.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Single cell suspensions were prepared from EBUS-TBNA samples of mediastinal lymph nodes (from 26 sarcoidosis and 16 lung cancer patients) and BAL fluid (50 ml saline instilled/retrieved three times). Flow cytometric analysis targeted surface markers (CD3, CD4, CD8, CD19, CD25) and FoxP3 expression on 1-3x10^4 cells per antibody combination. EBUS-TBNA was performed five to six times per patient. No therapeutic dose-response comparisons were reported, as the procedure was for diagnostic sampling.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Lymph nodes (EBUS-TBNA specimens), Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BAL fluid)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Ratio of T-lymphocyte subsets (flow cytometry analysis)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly more elevated in lymph nodes than in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (P<0.001); 84% of sarcoidosis patients showed a higher ratio in lymph nodes than BAL. Significantly higher in stage I than in stage II both in BAL fluid and lymph nodes (p = 0.014). Significantly higher in sarcoidosis when compared with lung cancer lymph node metastasis (p < 0.001); in age-matched patients (60-79 years), sarcoidosis 9.31     ± 4.15 vs lung cancer 1.70     ± 1.34 (p < 0.03). No significant difference with extrapulmonary lesions or gender.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicates the balance between helper (CD4) and cytotoxic (CD8) T-lymphocytes, crucial for immune response and regulation; CD4 positive T-lymphocytes play an important role in sarcoidosis pathogenesis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Diagnosis and staging of sarcoidosis; differential diagnosis of mediastinal lymphadenopathy between sarcoidosis and lung cancer; comparison of lymphocyte profiles in lymph nodes versus bronchoalveolar lavage fluid in sarcoidosis patients.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A higher ratio is indicative of sarcoidosis, differentiates it from lung cancer, and is associated with Stage I sarcoidosis. Used as a diagnostic and staging biomarker; reflects the immune status and helps elucidate immunopathology.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher in lung cancer compared to sarcoidosis. In sarcoidosis, the relative B-lymphocytes proportion (CD19+) was significantly higher than that of lung cancer metastatic lymph nodes (implying a lower CD3/CD19 ratio in sarcoidosis). No difference by gender or pathological classification (adenocarcinoma vs small cell carcinoma).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Represents the balance between T-lymphocytes (CD3+) and B-lymphocytes (CD19+), indicative of the cellular composition of the immune infiltrate and the type of immune response or malignancy.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Differential diagnosis of mediastinal lymphadenopathy between sarcoidosis and lung cancer.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Differentiates sarcoidosis from lung cancer based on the relative proportions of T and B lymphocytes; sarcoidosis shows a relatively higher B-lymphocyte proportion. Not influenced by gender or pathological classification in lung cancer.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Regulatory T cells (CD4+, CD25+, FoxP3 high) / Treg/CD4 T-lymphocytes ratio

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Did not differ between sarcoidosis and lung cancer samples. No significant difference was observed in the ratio of Treg/CD4 T-lymphocytes between sarcoidosis and lung cancer (Fig 4, Table 5). No difference by gender.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Regulatory T cells suppress immune responses, maintaining self-tolerance and preventing autoimmune disease and excessive immune responses. They have an important role in the pathogenesis of sarcoidosis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Comparison between sarcoidosis lymph nodes and lung cancer lymph nodes; differential diagnosis.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Lack of difference in Treg proportion suggests it might not be a distinguishing factor between sarcoidosis and lung cancer lymphadenopathy; not influenced by gender.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In sarcoidosis, lymphocytes in lymph nodes consisted of 56.6% CD4+ cells (SD: 13.8%) on average.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Helper T-lymphocytes, central to adaptive immune responses, orchestrating other immune cells.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Contributes to the overall lymphocyte profile used in sarcoidosis diagnosis and characterization.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In sarcoidosis, lymphocytes in lymph nodes consisted of 9.60% CD8+ cells (SD: 5.1%) on average.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cytotoxic T-lymphocytes, primarily responsible for killing infected or cancerous cells.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Contributes to the overall lymphocyte profile used in sarcoidosis diagnosis and characterization.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In sarcoidosis, lymphocytes in lymph nodes consisted of 29.5% CD19+ cells (SD 15.0%) on average. The relative B-lymphocytes proportion was significantly higher in sarcoidosis than that of lung cancer metastatic lymph nodes.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: B-lymphocytes, responsible for humoral immunity through antibody production.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A higher proportion in sarcoidosis contributes to its distinction from lung cancer.
